newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ bonds finish largely unchanged in thin trade.
newsitem.headline: NZ bonds finish largely unchanged in thin trade.

text.p: FUTURES PHYSICAL YIELD
10-YR T-BONDS (DEC) 92.09 (UNTRADED) 10-YR 7.98 (+0.02)
OVERNIGHT CASH 10.10 PCT (PREV 10.05) US 30-YR 6.81 (PREV 6.78)
* NZ bonds off slightly at close
* Market flow-driven three days out from general election
* Eurokiwi and samurai issuance helps sentiment
New Zealand bond yields finished a couple of basis points higher across the curve on Wednesday after another thin session, just three days out from a general election.
The bond market was slightly improved from its open, when it had looked quite vulnerable, dealers said.

"There was talk of selling overnight, concentrated in the long part of the curve, but once the long bond got above eight percent the market started to find some support. It got to a level where people thought it was okay to have another look at it," one said.
"As a result, with that support in the long bonds, the market has held in reasonably well, if not in fact coming back slightly better bid."
Short and mid bonds finished largely flat, although the 7/97s were off two to 8.90 percent and the 02/00s off one to 8.04. The 10-year bonds closed two points weaker at 7.98 percent.
In the money market, cash bumped up to 10.10 percent and the 90-day bank bills were up three to 10.03 percent as the Trade Weighted Index fell around 20 points to 65.82.
Dealers said trade was light and the market was extremely flow-driven, with few people taking positions ahead of Saturday's vote.
"Whatever the next flow is, that is the direction and feel of the market," one said.
"On the open with bonds coming back the market was trading on the offered side and felt horrible, but as soon as some buying came in the whole market just lurched the other way."
Recent political opinion polls have shown the main opposition Labour party and its potential coalition partners on the left closing in dramatically on the ruling conservative National party.

Dealers said beneath all the political uncertainty plaguing the market, a steady stream of issuing interest in samurais and eurokiwis continued as offshore players were drawn to New Zealand's high yields. Two NZ$100 million euros were set overnight in the short end of the curve.
